subject: Field report: customer retry behavior + SDK timeout override request
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Field report: intermittent streaming truncation + retry behavior (Alston Health)

Hi Dev / Marissa,

Quick summary: Alston Health reported repeated incidents where streaming responses are abruptly cut and their client sees a 503 with a Retry-After header in a subset of requests. Their integration uses our JS SDK (v1.5.2) with default retry behavior. The problem: the SDK aggressively retries immediately and opens duplicate sessions because the runtime-provided Retry-After header isn’t being surfaced to the application layer in the SDK, so their client retries before the service has recovered. This is causing doubled billable tokens and duplicate side-effects in their downstream system.

Attachments: I pulled the repro bundle they sent (alston_repro.zip) and the session logs (session-logs-20260922.txt). Relevant notes from the customer:
- Repro across multiple regions (us-west primarily)
- Occurs more often when prompt context > ~60k tokens (long-running conversation)
- They observe Retry-After: 6 (seconds) in the API response, but SDK ignores it and retries in ~500ms

Asks:
1) Runtime: can we ensure the Retry-After header from the HTTP response is propagated into the SDK surface so client code can act on it? If not, we should at least set a visible response property in the streaming event.
2) SDK/Product: expose per-request timeout & backoff override in the JS SDK (short-term patch) so customers can tune behavior for long contexts.
3) Ops/Runtime: triage whether the 503s are coming from fallback model routing or transient OOMs in the serving runtime (I suspect batching + long KV cache).

Customer impact: Mid-enterprise production — they are delaying a go-live and asked for a mitigation plan. Karthik, might need touch with customer success if we need to offer credits.

Next steps requested: Dev — please advise if you need a repro environment or extra traces. Marissa — prioritize visibility/SDK changes on roadmap?

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Re: Field report: intermittent streaming truncation + retry behavior (Alston Health)

Thanks Laura — digging in. Quick read on the attachments looks helpful. A few immediate clarifying Qs:
1) Can you confirm the exact SDK version and whether they are using the browser build or node? You mentioned v1.5.2 — that pre-dates our last retry fix (v1.5.6) so could be part of the problem.
2) When the 503 + Retry-After appears, do they get any runtime error codes in the body (e.g., KERNEL_OOM, BATCH_EXCEEDED)? The logs you attached show repeated partial responses interleaved with 503 lines but I need the raw HTTP traces (request-trace-20260922.har looks like it might contain that).

Preliminary thoughts: the runtime currently sets Retry-After on a subset of soft-fail responses (rate-limited or throttled endpoints). The pipeline that surfaces HTTP headers into streaming events is fragile in older SDKs — we did change behavior in 1.5.6 to surface a backoffHint value on the response event. Two paths:
- Short term: add an internal shim in the runtime to include Retry-After in the streaming framing (so older SDKs can see it). That should be a small change but needs validation.
- Medium term: SDK should standardize on a response.backoffHint and respect it before retrying.

I’ll try to reproduce on our staging cluster (us-west) with a long context replay. If I can reproduce I’ll file SUP-2147 and attach a runtime patch.

Dev

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Field report: intermittent streaming truncation + retry behavior (Alston Health)

Quick update from triage: reproduced in staging. Root cause appears to be a short-lived memory pressure event during KV cache compaction when a request includes a >60k token prefix. When the runtime falls back to a soft-shutdown of the worker we emit a 503 + Retry-After=6. The streaming framing code in the older client library (<=1.5.4) discards HTTP headers on close events; the new framing in 1.5.6 populates response.backoffHint for streamed close events.

Proposed path:
- Runtime: add immediate shim in the streaming proxy to inject a structured "x-rw-backoff" field into the streaming payload on soft-fail (1–2d; small change, risk low). This will make the backoff visible to all SDK versions.
- SDK/Product: schedule a 1.5.7 SDK patch to honor response.backoffHint by deferring the immediate retry for the recommended period (1 week triangular priority). Include a per-request option request.backoffOverride and request.timeoutMs that customers can pass.
- Customer mitigation: recommend they pin to 1.5.6 for now (which surfaces backoffHint) OR apply our suggested client-side retry wrapper to honor Retry-After in the HAR.

I’m opening SUP-2147 with the repro and heap snapshots. Laura — can you follow up with the customer and offer a short-term pin recommendation and ask if they'd like us to test against staging? Karthik — if this moves to credits or SLA impact, please advise.

Dev
